Fitting models

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code

Use this procedure to estimate parameters for one or more specified models from your observations. It saves fit records that the simulation and model-comparison templates can read, and can also generate responses and behavioral figures.

A model specification describes the mechanism, fixed values and bounds for fitted parameters. Optimizer settings describe how the search is conducted. The defaults fit three related models to the supplied observations using one pooled parameter set per model. You can instead select one model, a subset of participants, or separate participant fits.

For input conventions, see the data guide.

Configure this run

Start with data_path, output_dir, the observation selection and model_configs. For each model, inspect the component choices, parameters["fixed"], parameters["free"] and their bounds. A one-entry model_configs dictionary runs one model and is also a useful independent batch job.

pooled=True estimates one parameter set across the selected participants; pooled=False estimates participant-specific sets. subject_indices refers to positions in the sorted participant-ID list, not to the IDs themselves. Splitting a pooled fit into participant jobs changes the scientific analysis.

Set search effort in fit_hyperparams, separately from model parameters. The default optimizer settings can take substantial time. redo_fits=False loads an existing file at the chosen fit path without checking compatibility; a missing file still starts optimization. Reuse only a fit you know matches this run. Set both redo_sims and redo_figures to False for a fit-only run. Use a distinct output folder or run tag for a new specification.

Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.

Prepare the environment and inputs

Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.

project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. copy_example_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.

3 — Import packages 
import json

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from tabulate import tabulate

import jaxcmr
from jaxcmr import repetition
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.fitting import (
    make_scipy_loss_fn,
    parameters_for_subjects,
)
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.helpers import import_from_string
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, save_dict_to_hdf5
from jaxcmr.helpers import resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import save_figure
from jaxcmr.plotting import iter_analysis_figures
from jaxcmr.simulation import (
    load_matching_simulation,
    simulate_dataset,
)

Feature composition stays explicit here. feature_column selects the categorical feature, and concat_features=True combines categorical columns before semantic columns. When concatenation is requested, supply both feature arrays; otherwise the configured concatenation fails rather than substituting a different feature set.

4 — Define feature loading and model construction 
def load_features(spec):
    if spec.get("concat_features", False):
        semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path))
        categorical = np.load(
            resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path)
        )[:, int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1]
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path)) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path))[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return import_from_string(spec["model_factory"])(
        **{name: import_from_string(path) for name, path in spec["components"].items()}
    )

Inspect the work unit

The next cells select observations, create output locations and report the participants, models and free-parameter counts. trial_query controls the fitting observations. analysis_trial_query later controls behavioral displays; it does not change the observations used to fit the model.

Check the printed selection before launching optimization. target_directory, fit_dir, simulation_dir and figure_dir override their respective default locations; changing output_dir alone does not redirect an explicit override.

8 — Select the participant work unit and observation trials 
data_tag = data_tag or data_path.stem
subject_ids = np.unique(subjects)
if max_subjects:
    subject_ids = subject_ids[:max_subjects]
cohort_mask = generate_trial_mask(data, trial_query) & jnp.isin(
    data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids
)
if subject_indices:
    subject_ids = subject_ids[np.asarray(subject_indices, dtype=int)]
comparison_mask = cohort_mask & jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids)
selected_rows = np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(comparison_mask)).tolist()
if not selected_rows:
    raise ValueError("The configured selection contains no observations.")
if not model_configs:
    raise ValueError("Supply at least one model configuration.")

simulation_dir = (
    resolve_project_path(simulation_dir, root_path) if simulation_dir is not None else product_root / "simulations"
)
figure_dir = (
    resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else product_root / "figures/fitting"
)
for directory in [fit_dir, simulation_dir, figure_dir]:

11 — Prepare model-specific filenames and fit configurations 
fit_paths, simulation_paths, selections, fit_configurations = {}, {}, {}, {}
fitter_class = import_from_string(fit_alg_path)
loss_class = import_from_string(loss_fn_path)
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    search_settings = {
        **fit_hyperparams,
        "seed": model_spec["seed"],
        "bounds": parameter_config["free"],
    }
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    model_run_stem = f"{data_tag}_{model_name}_{run_tag}"
    stem = model_spec.get("output_stem", model_run_stem)
    if subject_indices:
        stem += "_sub" + "_".join(str(index) for index in subject_indices)
    fit_path = fit_dir / f"{stem}.json"
    if fit_path in fit_paths.values():
        raise ValueError("Each model needs a distinct output_stem.")
    fit_paths[model_name] = fit_path
    simulation_paths[model_name] = simulation_dir / f"{stem}.h5"
    selections[model_name] = comparison_mask
    configuration = {
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(cohort_mask)).tolist(),
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "parameters": parameter_config,
        "search_settings": search_settings,
        "pooled": pooled,
        "embedding_path": model_spec.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": model_spec.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": model_spec.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": model_spec.get("concat_features", False),
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    fit_configurations[model_name] = configuration

Fit or reuse saved results

Each model has a separate fit path and recorded configuration. With redo_fits=False, you are choosing to reuse the existing record at that path. You must establish that it uses the intended model and components, fixed/free parameters and bounds, participant IDs and selected observations, input data and features, and objective and stopping conventions. The notebook does not validate that compatibility. Recorded paths do not identify file contents, and missing metadata in an older record cannot establish how it was produced.

After changing data, code or the model specification, set redo_fits=True or choose a new output folder or run tag, and regenerate affected simulations. When an older record lacks model descriptions, the notebook uses the current settings in memory; reuse it only when you know those settings describe the original fit. It does not rewrite the reused file.

The notebook recalculates objectives from the physical parameter values and shows them beside the recorded values. For a reused fit, inspect these values yourself; agreement alone does not establish compatibility or search quality. For a newly computed fit, disagreement with the optimizer’s reported objective stops the run. In the supplied likelihood configuration, smaller negative log likelihood is better. Inspect bounds and search behavior as well as the final value.

12 — Prepare metadata for newly fitted records 
fit_metadata = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    stem = fit_paths[model_name].stem
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    fit_metadata[model_name] = {
        "name": stem,
        "model": model_name,
        "label": display_labels[model_name],
        "pooled": pooled,
        "data_tag": data_tag,
        "data_query": trial_query,
        "trial_query": trial_query,
        "run_tag": run_tag,
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": configuration["cohort_trial_indices"],
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "simulation_function": sim_alg_path,
        "fit_configuration": configuration,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "jax_version": jax.__version__,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "embedding_path": configuration["embedding_path"],
        "emotion_feature_path": configuration["emotion_feature_path"],
        "feature_column": configuration["feature_column"],
        "concat_features": configuration["concat_features"],
        "simulation_seed": simulation_seed,
        "simulation_repetitions": experiment_count,
    }
13 — Fit or load, recalculate the objective and save each model 
records = {}
fitted_now = set()
recalculated_objectives = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    model_factory = construct_model(model_spec)
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    if redo_fits or not fit_path.exists():
        fitter = fitter_class(
            data,
            features,
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            model_factory,
            loss_class,
            hyperparams=search_settings,
        )
        actual_subjects = np.unique(subjects[selected_rows])
        if pooled:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=-1)
        elif len(actual_subjects) == 1:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=int(actual_subjects[0]))
        else:
            fit_record = fitter.fit_subjects(comparison_mask)
        fitted_now.add(model_name)
    else:
        fit_record = json.loads(fit_path.read_text())
        # The caller establishes that this record matches the current run.
        # Fill missing legacy descriptions in memory; do not rewrite the file.
        for key in ("model_factory", "components", "loss_function", "data_path"):
            fit_record.setdefault(key, configuration[key])
        fit_record.setdefault("simulation_function", sim_alg_path)
        fit_record.setdefault("fit_configuration", configuration)
        fit_record.setdefault("pooled", pooled)
    expected_subjects = [-1] if pooled else np.unique(subjects[selected_rows]).tolist()
    if model_name in fitted_now and sorted(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]) != expected_subjects:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: fit rows do not match the selected participants."
        )

    # Evaluate the returned physical parameters independently of optimizer state.
    loss = loss_class(model_factory, data, features)
    free_parameter_names = tuple(parameter_config["free"])
    recalculated = []
    for subject_index, subject_id in enumerate(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]):
        subject_trials = (
            comparison_mask
            if pooled
            else comparison_mask & (data["subject"].ravel() == subject_id)
        )
        evaluate = make_scipy_loss_fn(
            loss,
            jnp.flatnonzero(subject_trials),
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            free_parameter_names,
        )
        free_parameter_values = jnp.asarray(
            [fit_record["fits"][key][subject_index] for key in free_parameter_names]
        )
        recalculated.append(float(evaluate(free_parameter_values)))
    if model_name in fitted_now and not np.allclose(
        fit_record["fitness"], recalculated, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-5
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: returned objective disagrees with recalculation."
        )
    if model_name in fitted_now:
        fit_record.update(fit_metadata[model_name])
        fit_record["recomputed_objective"] = recalculated
        if loss_fn_path.endswith("ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss") and pooled:
            fit_record["recomputed_nll"] = recalculated[0]
        fit_path.write_text(json.dumps(fit_record, indent=2) + "\n")
    records[model_name] = fit_record
    recalculated_objectives[model_name] = recalculated
14 — Display fitted parameters and independently recalculated objectives 
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    free_parameter_names = tuple(model_configs[model_name]["parameters"]["free"])
    recalculated = recalculated_objectives[model_name]
    print(display_labels[model_name], "—", fit_path)
    print(
        tabulate(
            {
                key: fit_record["fits"][key]
                for key in ["subject", *free_parameter_names]
            },
            headers="keys",
            floatfmt=".5g",
        )
    )
    print(
        tabulate(
            zip(fit_record["fits"]["subject"], fit_record["fitness"], recalculated),
            headers=["Subject", "Reported objective", "Recalculated"],
            floatfmt=".6f",
        )
    )
print("fit_paths =", {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in fit_paths.items()})

Generate responses when requested

This stage runs when simulations or behavioral figures are requested. parameters_for_subjects assigns the parameter rows by participant identity. A pooled parameter set is assigned to every selected participant; participant fits retain their assignments. experiment_count repeats each selected experiment, and simulation_seed controls sampling. Repetitions remain grouped under their original participant IDs.

The default simulator forces the observed recall counts. It can test predicted item choices and organization under those lengths, but matching lengths are imposed rather than predicted. Matching saved responses can be reused when redo_sims=False; a newly fitted model or different saved simulation settings requires fresh responses.

15 — Prepare participant parameters and simulation settings 
simulation_inputs = {}
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    if not (redo_sims or redo_figures):
        continue
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    features = load_features(fit_record)
    selected_trials = selections[model_name]
    is_pooled = fit_record.get("pooled", fit_record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1])
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selected_trials])
    subject_parameters = parameters_for_subjects(fit_record, participant_ids)
    configuration = {
        "fits": fit_record["fits"],
        "pooled": is_pooled,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"],
        "components": fit_record["components"],
        "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
        "embedding_path": fit_record.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": fit_record.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": fit_record.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": fit_record.get("concat_features", False),
        "seed": simulation_seed,
        "experiment_count": experiment_count,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    simulation_inputs[model_name] = {
        "model_factory": model_factory,
        "features": features,
        "parameters": subject_parameters,
        "trial_mask": selected_trials,
        "configuration": configuration,
    }
16 — Generate or reuse matching responses and save them 
simulations = {}
for model_name, prepared in simulation_inputs.items():
    model_factory = prepared["model_factory"]
    features = prepared["features"]
    subject_parameters = prepared["parameters"]
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    configuration = prepared["configuration"]
    simulation_path = simulation_paths[model_name]
    simulated = None
    if not redo_sims and model_name not in fitted_now:
        simulated = load_matching_simulation(simulation_path, configuration)
    if simulated is None:
        simulated = simulate_dataset(
            model_factory,
            data,
            features,
            subject_parameters,
            selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(configuration["simulation_function"]),
        )
        simulation_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(simulation_path))
        simulation_path.with_suffix(".json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **configuration,
                    "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
                    "jax_version": jax.__version__,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n"
        )
        print("Saved responses:", simulation_path)
    else:
        print("Loaded matching responses:", simulation_path)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = simulated.copy()
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[model_name] = simulated
print(
    "simulation_paths =",
    {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in simulation_paths.items()},
)

Inspect behavioral predictions

The configured analyses compare observations with saved simulations, using the selected observation subset and analysis-specific conditions. A model can improve the fitting objective while missing a behavioral pattern, so inspect measures relevant to your question.

filter_repeated_recalls affects these comparisons, not the original fit. The saved response files retain the simulated responses before this display filter.

17 — Prepare configured model and observation comparisons 
comparison_groups = []
if redo_figures and simulations:
    observed = data.copy()
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
    datasets = [observed, *simulations.values()]
    names = ["Observed", *[display_labels[name] for name in simulations]]
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "datasets": datasets,
            "labels": names,
            "base_masks": [comparison_mask, *[None for _ in simulations]],
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (dataset, label) in enumerate(zip(datasets, names)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "datasets": [dataset],
                "labels": [label],
                "base_masks": [comparison_mask if dataset_index == 0 else None],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )

Reuse the results

Use the printed fit_paths in the simulation template. If responses were generated, use simulation_paths in analysis templates and model comparison. Keep response JSON sidecars with their HDF5 files. New fit JSON files retain the fitted values, optimizer results, selected observations and provenance; the displayed objectives were recalculated independently.

For another question, change the model specification or selection in the settings cell and choose distinct output locations. For independent batch runs, vary the settings while retaining this procedure.
